placements.why: Script Extender support loads before anything that calls into it.
Loaders and fixers have to be in place before the mods they serve.
The interface framework a great many UI mods depend on.
A library, and Astra gives it a divider of its own.

Shared assets other mods read from.
MCM itself, ahead of the mods that register settings with it.
A framework other mods deliver items through.

A patcher, not a library: it rewrites what other mods added, so it has to run after them. Astra places it at 105 and the corpus puts it at the very end of the order holding it. Filing it as a Resource loaded it far too early.
Also a patcher, and Astra places it at 104 under Late Loaders.

requirementAliases.why: Published on Nexus as 'Vlad's Grimoire - Spell VFX Library' and shipped as a pak called VFX_Library_VladsGrimoire, so a mod requiring the short name matches neither. Same author on both, VladmirFFXI. Reported from a load order that had it installed and was told it was missing.
Nexus 18883 publishes as 'Mazzle's EZ-Documentation (MazzleDocs)' and the pak folder is Mazzle_Docs. Reported alongside Vlad's Grimoire by the same person, from a load order holding both.

requirementSatisfiedBy.why: Reported by a player told they were missing it while it was installed: the function was folded into Appearance Edit Enhanced and the requirement still names the old mod. The corpus cannot show this on its own, since Appearance Edit Enhanced is in most orders anyway, so co-occurrence proves nothing here.

Both deliver mod-added items to the player, and mods requiring one work with the other. Four of the five working orders that want it and lack it carry AV Item Shipment Framework, against it appearing in under a third of orders overall, so this is measured rather than assumed.
